notes.title: New Patches and Improvements
notes.notes:
Hello everyone! In there ongoing commitment to the game and community Dark Screen games have been working super hard. Listening to player feedback and acting upon it they have produced the following changes off of the back of your helpful feedback.

This update includes:
[list]
[*] - Glitch transition effect has been lowered or removed from sections of the game
[*] - The pause menu is now accessible in the tutorial
[*] - Re-spawn wait time has been lowered to 2 sec
[*] - Aerial recovery has been implemented with teleportation usable after grab
[*] - Further AI Balancing
[*] - Additional changes to slow motion effects
[/list]

We hope these additions imprve your Bounty Battle experience and we look forward to updating you further.

notes.title: Developer Insight - Bounty Points
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33417793/0ae4261d6b08b125a26ef285a42d281bfa0acafc.gif[/img]

Hey everyone,

Today we're sharing more insight from the development team behind Bounty Battle!

Even if in practise the game is closer to a traditional fighter: (life, energy and resources bar,) if I’m being honest, I liked the idea of being able to make an 'Ultimate Fighter' for the indie world. But the "brawler" system which consists of modifying power and/ or gravity according to a % did not please me more than that. I hated the idea of a copied/ pasted system that brought nothing new or personal to Bounty Battle’s core gameplay mechanics.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33417793/ef3e2c716c450b70a3859371ce17d61f608ee244.gif[/img]

I do not remember exactly how I came up with the idea of adding a bonus to the head of an opponent, but that added some nice background to the fighters, and also allowed us visually to find out who was the party leader. Then of course, that led me to wonder "what to do with this bonus?". Well, yes, this resource could replace energy and everything could have worked as bounty points. It's still a possibility that I don't rule out in a possible DLC or another version of the game, but in the end another idea took over, and then the decision was made to add an element of gameplay that is "the minions". Yes, this idea gave just as much added background to the characters, bringing with it an element of each character’s own universe, but also gave legitimacy to the Bounty Points system. 

Other mechanisms have (and will still) follow from this point system in order to allow for more strategic confrontations. The minions quickly rebalance certain characters, allowing players a complete gameplay experience. Even if the minions are in the background and not touchable, they can directly interact with and against the opponents.

We can't wait to share more news on Bounty Battle and share this great fighting game with you all.

notes.title: Developer Insight - Never Give Up
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33417793/f6892d29d75aac822ac2c417ffb8cf1fbd510f03.jpg[/img]

Hey everyone,

Today we're sharing more insight from the development team behind Bounty Battle!

There will always be little known gems from the indie world, and I am delighted with the idea of one day being able to help by uncovering games that in my eyes deserve to be discovered (or rediscovered). Of course the purpose of this dream would be to be able to add all the possible characters into Bounty Battle, but let's be realistic; there will be creators who will not wish to participate. For others, the rights relating to the use of the character are too complex and still at the end I cannot have infinite capacity to bring attention to every lost gem. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33417793/ba29ec00ca446487a0004a14bcbd2a14aab90534.jpg[/img]

Of course I have already been refused, and I understand well the creators who find it difficult to trust a stranger even if I have all the good will in the world. However, to stop there would be to restrict oneself to wanting only "big" guests, who in the end no longer represent what the independent world is in my eyes.

We can't wait to share more news on Bounty Battle and share this great fighting game with you all.

Why not add Bounty Battle to your Steam [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/860900/Bounty_Battle/]wishlist?[/url]

notes.title: Bounty Battle Delay
notes.notes:
We’re sorry to say that we’ve had to make the unfortunate decision to delay the launch of our upcoming All-Star Indie Fighter, Bounty Battle. 

Our goal to provide an amazing couch co-op experience to our community is within reach, but we felt that we still had significant improvements to make that we simply could not achieve without a slight delay. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33417793/fafb2814d41bfd1314f7dba6dd9ccc51e77d267d.gif[/img]

Our community's experience is of utmost importance to us, so keeping that in mind we decided to take the time we needed to deliver Bounty Battle as intended and intact. 

This means that Bounty Battle will no longer release on the 23rd July as previously announced. We will update the community as soon as we have a new release date to share with everyone!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33417793/d03960720163b64da9239ee215df6f6e94f4b56c.gif[/img]

We would like to take this time to thank you all for your patience and understanding while we resolve this.
Thank you,

notes.title: Developer Insight - Advent of Indie Gaming
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33417793/83334deabcdd6f10f4c4559fb435728018c2f457.jpg[/img]

Hey everyone,

Today we're sharing more insight from the development team from Bounty Battle!

To create a game like Bounty Battle, you must above all be passionate about gaming, especially independent video games. For me, indie gaming arrived in around 2005 and I was instantly intrigued, with the scene only continuing to expand since then. From the early 2000s, my decision was made, I would be an "indie" video game designer ... 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33417793/d2537eb84e5df1cf7985cea7a4406f9f998fe7c8.png[/img]

Fortunately, in these years, the popularization of creative tools and broadband allowed many independent and small studios to begin creating these magnificent independent games. After years of learning, modelling and development, it was finally time to embark on my own project. Of course we did not start a "major" project without breaking our teeth on models and other more or less functional prototypes, (including 2 familiar faces to Bounty Battle fans, Ollaf and R182). And for our game, once the concept was in place and the first contacts established, we quickly realized that the independent world is super friendly. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33417793/e821b439311c276fdf596e3c867f9bc4aa29e0e3.png[/img]

I can never thank enough all those who allowed me to realize this dream. But the will to make a game is not sufficient in itself, you have to give yourself the means to create your vision, and when you are independent, often the only way to do that, is to accept that it is going to be a massive undertaking, both in terms of effort and time, and that lifestyle often proves to be more difficult in practise.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33417793/44c717cef07caa34d4448710e22a8ea52c7dae41.png[/img]

We can't wait to share more news on Bounty Battle and share this great fighting game with you all.

notes.title: Hey everyone!
notes.notes:
This week we have some more insight from the developers into the development process of Bounty Battle!

Before starting this project, the developers of Bounty Battle were huge fans of "vanillaware" productions-it was one of the reasons they wanted to produce high-quality 2D assets. 

In Bounty Battle, special care was taken to bring guest characters and their worlds into the game. Some characters were easy to convert, because the games they came from looked similar aesthetically, or had similar gameplay mechanics. 

For other games it was more complicated, especially for the more minimalist or pixel art games. This process could take up to several weeks, creating all of the assets necessary to make the heroes and their attacks recognisable. 

The main thing during the development process was to keep a visual cohesion when the whole roster of the game is together.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33417793/55e61b9fa288cbf451e9d8b8666e5d7d4791e74b.png[/img]

notes.title: Bounty Battle Coming Summer 2020!
notes.notes:
Get Ready to Fight! After months of hard work, development and planning. We’re happy to say that Bounty Battle will be releasing this Summer on PC and console!

Check out the Dev team matches on the steam page!

Choose your favourite Indie heroes; from Dead Cells’ Prisoner to the Crusader from Dark Souls and battle it out in this one of a kind Fighter Frenzy! Each fighter comes with their own Minion companion and unique abilities. Battle across levels inspired from the fighters’ native game worlds with up to 3 other players.

Bounty Battle features over 25 characters from over 20 different Indie classics.

Features:
•	A host of game modes including a Tournament mode, Local-Multiplayer, Tutorial and Training Room to master your character
•	Over 20 Fighters from your favourite Indie games! Each with their own move set and special attacks
•	Each Fighter has their very own minion to summon and join the fight
•	Over 10 different arenas to battle on – some inspired by the worlds of their fighters
•	Multiple color and pallet swap options to fight in style!

Be sure to add Bounty Battle to your Wishlist and check out the latest trailer - [previewyoutube=jD4izZy5JSA;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]
